2. What the Service is

Pawstcard lets a pet sitter keep client and pet records on the sitter's own phone, record a visit (photos, tapped facts, optional walk route), have an AI write a draft report, review and approve it, and send a link to a web page of that report to the pet's owner. No account is required; the app signs you in anonymously only to upload what you send. Your data on the phone can be saved to a backup file you control.

3. Using the Service

You may use the Service for your own pet-sitting work, including paid work. You agree not to:

  • enter or send content that is unlawful, that infringes someone's rights, or that harms or harasses others;
  • send photos or information about a person's home, pets or contact details without having the right to, or contrary to what the pet's owner agreed [confirm T5: whether the terms should require the sitter to hold the client's consent — legal check];
  • copy, scrape or republish the Service or a substantial part of its design, text or code, or use them to train a commercial model, without our written permission;
  • interfere with the Service, probe or test its security, or send automated requests at a rate that burdens it — including calling the AI feature outside the app;
  • reverse-engineer or tamper with the app, or bypass its limits or any payment or subscription check (except where law allows).

We may remove a sent page or limit use if we reasonably believe these rules are broken, or if the law or a store requires. We will tell you by email where we can.

4. Your content and your responsibility

  1. You own it. The photos, names, notes and reports you create remain yours. You allow us (and the providers that run the Service, listed in the privacy policy) to process, store and display them only as needed to run the features you use — resizing photos, asking the AI for a draft, hosting the page you send, and showing it to whoever has the link.
  2. A sent page is open to anyone with its link. Pawstcard pages are not password-protected and are not listed or searchable; anyone you or the recipient share the link with can open it and may save or forward it. Send it only to people you intend to.
  3. You approve what is sent. The AI writes only a draft from the facts you tap, the photos you add and your notes; you review and approve it before it is sent. The text you send is your report to your client. The medication line is generated from your records, not by the AI.
  4. Removing a sent page. Deleting a visit or client in the app removes it from your phone, but not the web page already uploaded. To remove a sent page, write to us at the address in section 12 with the link [confirm T6: deletion procedure and response time — same as privacy P16; the product requirement of invalidating a link from the app is not built (privacy P17)].
  5. Backups. A backup file is created on your request and stays with you; keep it safe. Restoring a backup replaces the data in the app after you confirm.

5. AI-written drafts

The report drafts are produced by an AI model (Google Gemini through Firebase AI Logic). AI can be wrong or omit things, even though the app tells it to use only the facts you provide. You are responsible for checking a draft before you send it. The AI label shown to the owner follows the app's own wording [confirm T7: wording of the AI note on the sent page and legal check that it meets Korea's AI Basic Act — see DECISIONS D-004]. Use of the AI feature may be limited by a monthly counter or by cost safeguards, and may change [confirm T8: any monthly limit and price tier, if the AI feature becomes paid].

6. Paid features and in-app purchases

The current version has no in-app purchase or subscription (no billing library in the app). If we add paid features, we will first update these terms and the privacy policy, show the price, billing period, automatic renewal and how to cancel before you pay, and follow the refund rules of the App Store or Google Play; we will not receive card details [confirm T9: planned paid features/prices — Davy decision; then adopt the canon clauses: subscription notice, minors, withdrawal and refunds, restore purchases, 30 days' notice and refund of the unused period when a paid service ends].

7. Links, third parties and weather/map data

The app and pages rely on third-party services (Google Firebase, Google Maps Static Maps, Open-Meteo for weather). They run under their own terms and we are not responsible for their availability or accuracy. Weather and route maps are for convenience and may be incomplete or wrong. The app contains no advertising.

8. No professional advice

Pawstcard is a reporting tool for pet sitters. Nothing in the app or in AI drafts is veterinary, medical, behavioural or safety advice, and the app does not monitor a pet's health. If a pet seems unwell, contact a veterinarian or local emergency service. Pawstcard is not a party to the agreement between a sitter and a pet owner and is not responsible for the sitting service.

9. Availability, and limits of liability

We provide the Service “as is” and “as available”, with no promise that it will be error-free, uninterrupted or up to date. Because pages are stored with third-party hosting, we cannot promise a sent link will always open, or how long it stays available [confirm T10: how long sent pages are kept — same as privacy P5]. We may change or suspend free features. If we change, suspend or end a paid service, we give at least 30 days' notice and refund the unused part of any period you already paid for under the relevant store's policy.

To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, for loss from using or being unable to use the Service, from the content of AI drafts you sent without checking, or from third-party services. This does not apply to loss caused by our intent or gross negligence, and nothing here releases us from that liability. Nothing here limits liability that cannot be limited by law, or mandatory consumer rights where you live.
